parts:
Sharon-

It sounds like your measurements have been rounded but that is only a=20
guess. AIC is useful for selecting a model from competing models and=20
goodness of fit provides a guide to the adequacy of model fit. I use=20
the term "guide" because as you see, the results can depend on the cut=20
points although not usually that much. The K-S and Cramer-VonMises test=20
are 2 alternatives if your distances are not collected in intervals, but=20
they can be sensitive to rounding. You should use the gof tests to=20
identify important problem areas with the model fit/data collection.

--jeff

parts:
Sharon, if you rely on chi-sq gof, you need to choose cutpoints well away f=
rom favoured rounding distances. If you do, you shouldn't see that level of=
sensitivity. Without careful choice of cut-points, gof isn't very useful i=
f you have heaping. It's not telling you about model mis-fit - just that yo=
u have a problem with the data.
